props.title: Mamma Mia!
props.initialSlug: Musical romance fueled by ABBA hits and secret dads

sections.content: Mamma Mia! revolutionized the jukebox musical film genre by weaving ABBA's infectious pop hits into a sun-soaked Greek island romance. Following the massive success of the 1999 stage musical, director Phyllida Lloyd created a star-studded adaptation that proved Hollywood musicals could still draw massive audiences. The film's success paved the way for other stage-to-screen musical adaptations like Les Misérables (2012) and Into the Woods (2014), while its carefree spirit influenced lighter fare like Pitch Perfect (2012).

sections.content: Meryl Streep's commitment to the role of Donna validated the movie musical for a new generation of A-list actors. Her fearless performance, especially in "The Winner Takes It All," showed that dramatic actors could embrace the genre's demands without sacrificing credibility. This opened doors for other serious actors in musicals, from Emma Stone in La La Land (2016) to Hugh Jackman in The Greatest Showman (2017).

The film's visual style created a template for modern movie musicals set in real locations rather than soundstages. Like Moulin Rouge! (2001) before it, Mamma Mia! proved that musical numbers could work in actual settings, influencing films like In the Heights (2021) and Yesterday (2019). The Greek island of Skopelos became a major tourist destination, showing how musical films could impact real-world locations. SUBHEAD: The ABBA Renaissance

sections.content: Mamma Mia! sparked renewed interest in ABBA's music, leading to countless covers, tributes, and eventually the band's own comeback. The film's success directly influenced the creation of jukebox musicals like Rock of Ages (2012) and Jersey Boys (2014), though none matched its box office impact. The 2018 sequel Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again proved the franchise's enduring appeal, while incorporating deeper emotional themes alongside its predecessor's jubilant energy.
